orientation.theme: Whether glyphosate's regulatory safety status reflects sound science or an industry-shaped system that ignores complete formulations, mixtures, microbiome effects, and low-dose chronic harms.
orientation.thesis: The article endorses Michael Antoniou's argument that glyphosate is deceptively toxic and remains accepted as safe because regulators rely on industry-influenced, incomplete testing that understates real-world exposure and harm.

thesisHinge.proposition: Regulatory conclusions of glyphosate safety depend on incomplete and industry-influenced evidence that fails to represent actual exposures and low-dose chronic effects.

orientation.notes: The article is a strongly favorable report of Antoniou's position. The industry plant-pathway argument is preserved as an opponent proposition and linked to the microbiome rebuttal.

grounding.verbatimExcerpt: Glyphosate has remained one of the world’s most widely used herbicides not because the science supports its safety, but because industry has shaped nearly every step of the regulatory process, molecular geneticist and toxicologist Michael Antoniou, Ph.D. , said this week. In an interview on “ The Corbett Report ,” Antoniou outlined what he sees as the biggest failures that have kept the “deceptively toxic” herbicide on the market despite a growing body of independent research linking it to serious health risks. Antoniou, professor emeritus at King’s College London, spent more than a decade leading pesticides research and building a group he described as “a world leader in glyphosate herbicide toxicology.” He said industry’s influence extends from the studies regulators rely on and the products they test to the exposure limits they consider safe. “That is not science,” he said. “That is really an act of deception.”

argumentUnits.canonicalAtomicProposition: Glyphosate remains widely used because industry has shaped the regulatory process rather than because safety science supports it.
scopeQualifiers: Antoniou's assessment of global glyphosate regulation
